title: Playground to Dolly's
story: Start downtown, let everyone burn off a first round of energy at the playground, then roll out Main St to where the path begins at W Main. From there it is flat, shaded pavement the whole way northeast past the depot, and the new bridge at the far end drops you right at Dolly's window. It is the ride most Brevard kids learn the path on.

stops.name: Silvermont Park
stops.note: Playground, pavilion, and shade before you start.

stops.name: Railroad Depot Repair Stand
stops.note: Parking and restrooms here. Top off tires — it saves a walk later.

stops.name: Mid-Path Fix-It Stand
stops.note: Halfway breather. Water filler beside the stand.

stops.name: Dolly's Dairy Bar
stops.note: Over the new bridge from the north end. Mostly flat, 25 minutes from town.

title: Ninja Park and Smash Burgers
story: Roll out Main St to the trailhead and take the flat path northeast past the depot and the mid-path stand to Jameson's Joy, where the ninja course gets the wiggles out. Double back a few hundred feet to the Cherry Street Greenway and follow it east to the CHUBwagon, the food truck parked at the brewery every day. Burgers, chicken tenders, grilled cheese and a kids' cheeseburger, eaten on the big lawn. Same path home.

stops.name: Railroad Depot Repair Stand
stops.note: Restrooms and parking. Last easy bathroom stop before lunch.

stops.name: Mid-Path Fix-It Stand
stops.note: Water filler beside the stand — top up bottles here.

stops.name: Jameson's Joy (Ninja Park)
stops.note: Open 24 hours and fully accessible. A lap or two before anyone eats.

stops.name: CHUBwagon at Oskar Blues
stops.note: Turn back to the greenway and ride east. Racks and a repair stand at the taproom door.

kids.name: CHUBwagon
kids.note: Turn back to the greenway and ride east. Bike racks and a repair stand at the end.

kids.story: Roll out Main St to the trailhead and take the flat path northeast past the depot and the mid-path stand to Jameson's Joy, where the ninja course gets the wiggles out. Double back a few hundred feet to the Cherry Street Greenway and follow it east to the CHUBwagon food truck. Burgers, chicken tenders, grilled cheese and a kids' cheeseburger, eaten on the big lawn. Same path home.

title: Steamers and Swings
story: The shortest ride in the app and the flattest. Pick up steamed sandwiches and hot dogs at Sully's on E Main, walk the bikes to the courthouse and ride the Main St sidewalk out to the trailhead. The path takes you to The Yard on Railroad Ave, with a playset, a kids' bike park and ice cream for afters, and Depot Park and its restrooms are just past it. Prefer pizza? HomeSlyce on King St does it by the slice.

stops.name: Sully's Steamers
stops.note: 33 E Main St. Order to go and eat at The Yard, or sit down first.

stops.name: The Yard
stops.note: Playset, kids' bike park and ice cream at 284 Railroad Ave.

stops.name: Railroad Depot Repair Stand
stops.note: Restrooms, parking and a pump. Turn around here.

title: Bike to School Day
tagline: Ride in with the Brevard Bike Alliance
story: Twice a year the Brevard Bike Alliance sponsors a Bike, Walk & Roll to School Day — National Bike to School Day each May, and again in October — with group rides and meet-ups at Pisgah Forest Elementary, Brevard Elementary, Brevard Middle, Brevard High, Mountain Sun and Pisgah Collective. This is the one route where the path does the whole job: meet at Depot Park, ride northeast, and middle schoolers turn off at Fisher Rd while elementary riders keep going to Pisgah Forest. Dates and meet-up points for each school are announced by the Alliance at brevardbikealliance.org.

stops.name: Railroad Depot Repair Stand
stops.note: Meet here. Pump, restrooms and parking at Depot Park.

stops.name: Brevard Middle School
stops.note: Turn off at Fisher Rd and take the short connector to the school.

stops.name: Pisgah Forest Elementary School
stops.note: Right beside the path. Flat the whole way from the depot.

title: Ball Field to Library Loop
tagline: A whole Saturday on two wheels
story: Park at the ball fields and make a day of it. The Ninja Park is right there, so start with a lap of the course before anyone has earned lunch. Then it is a straight, flat run down the path into town — lock up on Main, eat, and roll the last few blocks to the library to trade in a stack of books. The ride home is the same path in reverse, with an ice cream stop at The Yard before you load the bikes.

stops.name: Brevard Ball Fields
stops.note: Park here off Ecusta Rd. Restrooms and plenty of room to get sorted.

stops.name: Jameson's Joy (Ninja Park)
stops.note: Right beside the fields. Burn off the first round of energy here.

stops.name: Lunch downtown
stops.note: Lock up on Main — everything is within a block of where the path lands.

stops.name: Transylvania County Library
stops.note: A few blocks south on S Gaston. Racks out front, books for the ride home.

stops.name: The Yard
stops.note: Ice cream and the kids’ bike park on Railroad Ave — the last stop before the fields.

title: Taproom Traverse
tagline: The Hub to downtown, all downhill in spirit
story: Adults only, and best started early enough that the last leg is still light. Begin at the Pisgah Tavern inside The Hub, roll down past Dolly’s and over the new bridge, then pick up the path and work your way back toward town — Ecusta on the Ecusta Rd side, Oskar Blues off Mountain Industrial, the King St row in the middle, and Brevard Brewing to finish on E Main. One direction, flat the whole way, and it ends where the food is.

stops.name: The Hub & Pisgah Tavern
stops.note: Start at the forest gateway. One pour, then point the bikes downhill.

stops.name: Ecusta Brewing Company
stops.note: Steps off the path at 451 Ecusta Rd. First stop after the bridge.

stops.name: Oskar Blues (Tasty Weasel Taproom)
stops.note: Big lawn and food on Mountain Industrial. The natural mid-ride sit-down.

stops.name: Squatch Bikes & Brews
stops.note: King St row. Noblebräu and Griffon & Sphynx are both a short walk from here.

stops.name: Brevard Brewing Company
stops.note: Finish on E Main, a block from everything. Walk from here.

title: Ride to a Downtown Festival
tagline: Skip the parking, arrive on two wheels
story: Festival weekends turn downtown parking into a sport nobody wins. The path carries all the way to W Main instead, so you arrive a block from the tents. Leave from the Pisgah Forest end, ride southwest past the depot into town, and lock up on Main. Coming home after dark is easy, but bring a light — the far end is unlit by design.

stops.name: Pisgah Forest End
stops.note: Free parking near Ecusta Rd. Fills by late morning on festival days.

stops.name: Mid-Path Fix-It Stand
stops.note: Halfway breather, with water.

stops.name: Railroad Depot Park
stops.note: Lock up here. Restrooms, pavilion, and the ballerina sculpture.

stops.name: Rocky's Grill & Soda Shop
stops.note: Open late on festival nights. Shorter line after the band starts.

title: Gateway to Pisgah
story: The network gets you all the way to the national forest without riding Hwy 64. Pick up the path at W Main, ride the full length northeast past the depot, then cross the new bridge and carry on past Dolly’s to the forest gateway, where the shop and the tavern sit side by side. Flat, paved, and separated nearly the whole way.

stops.name: Earth Mountain
stops.note: Borrow a floor pump before you go. Ask what the forest roads are doing.

stops.name: Pisgah Forest Repair Stand
stops.note: Last water and tools before the bridge crossing.

stops.name: Dolly's Dairy Bar
stops.note: First thing on the far side of the bridge. Obligatory.

stops.name: The Hub & Pisgah Tavern
stops.note: Forest gateway. Shop on one side, tavern on the other.

kids.name: The Hub
kids.note: Forest gateway. Bike shop, and the end of the pavement.

kids.story: The network gets you all the way to the national forest without riding Hwy 64. Pick up the path at W Main, ride the full length northeast past the depot, then cross the new bridge and carry on past Dolly’s to the forest gateway and The Hub bike shop. Flat, paved, and separated nearly the whole way.

title: Concert Night at the Music Center
story: Music Center nights turn the west side of town into a parking problem, so leave the car at the ball fields instead. The path runs flat and straight from there into downtown — time it so you arrive with an hour to eat on Main — then it is a short climb out Probart to the Music Center. Bring a blanket, bring lights for the ride home, and you will be past the traffic before it starts moving.

stops.name: Brevard Ball Fields
stops.note: Park off Ecusta Rd. Free, and empty on concert nights.

stops.name: Railroad Depot Park
stops.note: Restrooms and a repair stand, roughly two thirds of the way in.

stops.name: Dinner on Main
stops.note: The path lands a block off Main. Lock up once and walk to whatever is open.

stops.name: Brevard Music Center
stops.note: Short climb out Probart. Lawn seating, and far easier to leave on a bike.

stops.name: The Yard
stops.note: If it is still open on the way back, ice cream on Railroad Ave.

title: Downtown to the River
tagline: Main St to the campground parking
story: The long one, and the reason the network matters. Start downtown, take the path its full length past the depot, and cross the road at Lowe’s into Pisgah Forest. Past Dolly’s it turns to gravel and follows the Davidson River — Sycamore Flats, then the pull-off where everyone gets in, then the parking lot by the campground, which is as close as wheels get. The air changes about a mile in. Just under six miles out.

stops.name: Railroad Depot Repair Stand
stops.note: Top off here. It is the last full repair stand before the forest.

stops.name: Lowe’s Crossing
stops.note: The path crosses the road here — dismount, cross, and pick it up on the far side.

stops.name: Dolly's Dairy Bar
stops.note: Over the bridge. Worth stopping on the way out and the way back.

stops.name: Sycamore Flats
stops.note: Picnic tables under the sycamores, right on the river.

stops.name: River Pull-Off
stops.note: A flat dirt landing under a leaning tree, where the bank shelves straight into the water. The one to stop at if you came to swim.

stops.name: Davidson River Campground
stops.note: The turnaround, where the path meets the parking lot. The campground is across it — restrooms, water and river access — and this is the closest public parking to it.

title: The Hub to Bracken and Back
tagline: Pavement out, dirt over the mountain, pavement home
story: The big loop, and the only ride here that needs knobby tires. Roll out of The Hub, down the bridge connector and the full length of the path into town, then out Probart to the Bracken Mountain trailhead. From there it is natural-surface singletrack up and over the ridge into the national forest, dropping you out at the campground end of the forest path. Pick up the campground connector back past Sycamore Flats, and you are on pavement again for the last stretch to Dolly’s and home. Plan a full day, carry water, and check trail conditions before you go.

stops.name: The Hub & Pisgah Tavern
stops.note: Start and finish here. Check conditions at the shop before you roll out.

stops.name: Bracken Mountain Trailhead
stops.note: End of Probart St. Last chance to bail back into town if the legs are not there.

stops.name: Bracken Mountain Trail
stops.note: Natural-surface singletrack over the ridge into the forest. Mountain bike only.

stops.name: Davidson River Campground
stops.note: You pop out at the far end of the campground connector. Water and restrooms across the parking lot.

stops.name: Sycamore Flats
stops.note: Picnic tables and the river on the way back — a good place to eat.

stops.name: Dolly's Dairy Bar
stops.note: A couple of hundred feet from the finish. Earned.

title: End to End
tagline: The whole path, W Main to Pisgah and back
story: The full length of the Brevard Bike Path in one go: 4 miles of old rail grade each way, from W Main out to the Pisgah Forest end, flat the entire distance, with the long shaded stretch in the middle where it stays cool even in August. Most riders do it in a morning, stop downtown for lunch, and coast home in the afternoon.

stops.name: Railroad Depot Repair Stand
stops.note: Start here — parking, restrooms, and a stand to top off before a long day.

stops.name: Mid-Path Fix-It Stand
stops.note: Mile 2.3 bail-out if something needs fixing: pump, chain tool and water. CykelWorx is back downtown on S Broad St.

stops.name: Oskar Blues Brewery
stops.note: Near the turnaround. Food, shade, and somewhere to sit.

kids.name: CHUBwagon
kids.note: Near the turnaround. Food truck, shade, and somewhere to sit.

stops.name: Pisgah Forest Repair Stand
stops.note: Turnaround point. Working pump gauge and shaded benches.

title: Pisgah Short Track Social
tagline: Small-town race night by the Depot
story: Four Wednesday evenings around the Fourth of July, Brevard races bikes. Nature Trails, LLC, the trail builders on Commerce St, hosts the Pisgah Short Track Social on its short-track features beside Depot Park: laps for every age, bike games and plenty of friendly heckling. It's free, and donations go to Pisgah Area SORBA for trail upkeep. In 2026 it ran June 17 to July 8 from 5:30pm; dates change each summer, so check before you go. Ride up the path from W Main, air up at the Depot repair stand and cross to Commerce St. The Yard is on the way home.

stops.name: West Main trailhead
stops.note: Start where the path meets W Main, by the yellow bollard.

stops.name: Railroad Depot Repair Stand
stops.note: Pump the tires and use the restrooms before the start.

stops.name: Nature Trails short track
stops.note: On Commerce St across from the Depot Park sign. Racing starts at 5:30pm on series Wednesdays.

stops.name: The Yard
stops.note: Ice cream on the ride back.

title: Earth Mountain Shop Ride
tagline: A group ride, then hot chocolate
story: Earth Mountain Bicycle, the Trek shop at 66 E Main, runs family-friendly group rides. Look for the bike-and-dog mural on its wall. In December 2024 it was a Letters to Santa ride at 4pm on a Saturday, with hot chocolate and cookies back at the shop. Ask in the shop or check its Facebook page for this season's rides. Any day, the easy version is the same loop: walk the bikes along Main St to Kilwins, then ride out the path to The Yard and back. Main St is too busy to ride with kids, but the walk is short.

stops.name: Earth Mountain
stops.note: 66 E Main. Meet at the shop, then walk the bikes along Main St to Kilwins. It's too busy to ride with kids.

stops.name: The Yard
stops.note: Turn around here, or stop for the kids' bike park.

stops.name: Back at Earth Mountain
stops.note: Hot chocolate and cookies after the holiday ride.

title: Bike to the Rock Gym
story: Ride from the path to the climbing wall. Leave the path at W Main, turn down England St and W Jordan, then follow S Broad to Brevard Rock Gym at 240-B S Broad. Open climb is Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday 5–8pm and Saturday 2–5pm. It's bouldering only, with no ropes, and you can get a day pass and rental shoes at the desk. Tae Kwon Do is next door, and the library's repair stand across S Broad has a pump for the ride home.

stops.name: West Main trailhead
stops.note: Leave the path where it meets W Main, by the yellow bollard.

stops.name: W Jordan at S Broad
stops.note: Stay on this side of S Broad. The gym is on the same side, so there's no need to cross US 64.

stops.name: Brevard Rock Gym
stops.note: Open climb Tue, Wed, Fri 5–8pm and Sat 2–5pm. Day passes and rental shoes at the desk.

title: Sculpture on the Path
tagline: Seventeen sculptures in one loop from the Depot
story: Seventeen of the 25 pieces on the Brevard Sculpture Walk, in one loop from Depot Park. Start with Ballerina Angelina, then ride the path past the Lumberyard's cows and turn down Whitmire St to the Methodist church. Across N Broad, Brevard College's lawn has a saxophone, a violin and an 18-foot banjo. Follow N Broad to the courthouse's Red Wolf and Elk, then go out E Main past the Earth Mountain bike mural to the otter at the Visitor Center and the fox at St Philip's. Head down Gaston St to the library's heron, then out S Broad to the trout, the owl and the deer. Come back past the turkey, take Jordan and England Sts to City Hall's bear and squirrels, and ride W Main and the path back to the Depot. N Broad and Main St are busy, so ride the sidewalks with kids and walk the bikes on Main.

stops.name: Ballerina Angelina
stops.note: Park at Jimmy Harris Railroad Depot Park. Fifteen feet of found objects by Stefan “Steebo” Bonitz, plus restrooms, a repair stand and the donor bricks.

stops.name: Cows
stops.note: Aaron Alderman's herd grazes in the Lumberyard behind the old Brevard Lumber Company sign, where you leave the path for Whitmire St.

stops.name: First United Methodist
stops.note: Cross N Caldwell here. The playground is open to the public weekday afternoons.

stops.name: Saxophone, Violin and Banjo
stops.note: Kyle Van Lusk's giant instruments on the Brevard College lawn along N Broad. The banjo is 18 feet tall.

stops.name: Red Wolf and Elk
stops.note: On the courthouse lawn at Main and Broad. The wolf is made from more than 2,000 slivers of steel.

stops.name: Otter
stops.note: Splash the Otter in the fountain at the Visitor Center, 175 E Main. You pass the Earth Mountain bike mural on the way.

stops.name: Red Fox and Tim Murray abstract
stops.note: At St Philip's Episcopal, a little further along E Main: a bronze fox peeking over rocks by the parking lot, and an abstract piece in the memory garden. Turn back here for Gaston St.

stops.name: Great Blue Heron
stops.note: In the rain garden in front of the library on Gaston St. The repair stand outside has a pump.

stops.name: Trout, Owl and Red Deer
stops.note: Along S Broad south of the library: a 12-foot spinning trout, an owl up high at 320 S Broad, and a deer at South Broad Park. The Arts Council's Horses and Golden Eagle are a block west on S Caldwell.

stops.name: Wild Turkey
stops.note: Bronze, on the First Citizens Bank lawn at W Morgan and S Broad.

stops.name: Black Bear and White Squirrels
stops.note: In front of City Hall, 95 W Main, by way of W Jordan and England St. Find the bee on the bear's nose.

stops.name: Back to the Depot
stops.note: Rejoin the path at W Main and ride it back past The Yard.
